notes: Identity assessment: the supplied canonical text is a full empirical replication manuscript with results and supplementary material, headed “Essential moral self remains unchallenged: Successful replication of Strohminger and Nichols (2014) with extensions comparing morality to ideology and religion”. Title-page authors are Chung Hin (Samson) Wong and Gilad Feldman (opposite order to the neutral reference); p. 4 and p. 21 explicitly identify project https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/G2ZV6. This supports primary-report identity; publication year 2025 is not independently established from the supplied text. No PDF was supplied. Target correspondence is based on Study 1, Brain Transplant, the named Morality - Amnesia contrast, the identity-change outcome and p. 38 locator, not row order or numeric agreement. Analytic contrast-group N derivation: 143 + 140 = 283 participants, with mutually exclusive assignment established by p. 25. The Tukey comparison is fitted within a seven-group ANOVA; its pooled-error model includes 143 + 140 + 140 + 141 + 138 + 143 + 138 = 983 participants (Table 15), so 283 denotes the contrasted groups rather than the entire pooled-error model. Full-sample analysis is the primary analysis per p. 35; do not substitute the supplementary exclusion analysis. Table 16 prints ds = 0.49, 95% CI [0.25, 0.73], t = 4.12, df = 976, p < .001, all for the same named contrast.
